title: Ancient Greece and Democracy
text: Ancient Greece was a northeastern Mediterranean civilization, flourishing from around 800 BCE to 146 BCE when Rome conquered it. Greek city-states (poleis), particularly Athens and Sparta, developed distinct political systems. Athens is credited with developing the first democracy around 508 BCE under Cleisthenes. Greek contributions to philosophy (Socrates, Plato, Aristotle), science (Archimedes, Euclid), and literature (Homer, Sophocles) profoundly shaped Western civilization. The Persian Wars (499–449 BCE) and the Peloponnesian War (431–404 BCE) were major conflicts. Alexander the Great's conquests spread Greek culture across the known world in a period called the Hellenistic Age.
